issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) for managing the shared stock, but the provided solution implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). Additionally, the template's Main example calls shop.acceptSupplyDelivery(...) as an instance method (non-static invocation). This creates a structural inconsistency in the expected method name and how it should be invoked (static vs. instance), which will confuse students implementing the API and may cause tests or examples to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery and keep it static, and update any sample code to call SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(...) as a static method; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to specify receiveDelivery as the required static method name and change the sample in Main to call SealSaloon.receiveDelivery(...). Also correct the sample invocation in Main to use the static form (SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery or SealSaloon.receiveDelivery) if the method is intended to be static.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a static supply-delivery method named acceptSupplyDelivery(...), but the solution implements this functionality under a different name, receiveDelivery(...). This mismatch (acceptSupplyDelivery vs receiveDelivery) refers to the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery into the shared stock) and can confuse students trying to map the requirements to the implementation or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for the supply delivery operation across all artifacts. Rename receiveDelivery(...) in SealSaloon to acceptSupplyDelivery(...) (keeping it static and with the same signature), or add a static acceptSupplyDelivery(...) wrapper that delegates to receiveDelivery(...). Also update any references (e.g., Main) to the chosen name so students can clearly map the requirement to implementation.
